Subject: Re: Spike & degraded checkout latency 4/24 - request for window audit and remedy

Folks — I pulled the cluster control plane and serving traces for the requested UTC hour. Preliminary findings:

- Observed two short autoscaler misfires at 02:12:17–02:14:02 UTC and 02:22:05–02:24:00 UTC where node eviction events caused increased queueing and a KV-cache miss storm for one shard serving BrightCart's region. Cumulative effective degraded window (latency elevated beyond our 99th percentile threshold) is ~18 minutes. We also saw a small number of 503s (~0.9% of requests) during the eviction windows tied to connection churn.
- Root cause: a race in the autoscaler health-check logic during a transient control-plane GC which caused two nodes to be drained prematurely; the runtime then backfilled but there was a ~30s tail each event while KV caches warmed.

I’ve attached a trimmed trace bundle (internal reference: INT-TRACE-20270424-brightcart.zip) to our drive link for engineers and compliance. Proposed immediate mitigations:
- Patch the autoscaler health-check timeout to avoid GC-triggered false negatives (hotfix in staging now).
- Add a short-lived cache-warm thread for critical shards during scale-up to reduce the warming tail.

Proposed verified window to return to the customer: 2027-04-24T02:12:17Z to 2027-04-24T02:30:00Z (18 minutes  - combines both events). I will prepare an internal RCA and postmortem targeted for 2027-05-03.

Ravi — thank you for your patience. We completed the server-side audit and confirm a verified degraded window of 2027-04-24T02:12:17Z to 2027-04-24T02:30:00Z (18 minutes total). Summary and proposed remedy below:

What we observed:
- Two autoscaler-driven node drain events caused elevated tail latency and a small set of 503s during the combined 18-minute window.
- Impact on BrightCart: between 02:12–02:30 UTC we measured a 95th percentile jump and ~0.9% increased 503 rate on requests routed to the affected shard.

Proposed remedy (prorated calculation):
- SLA reference: monthly uptime SLA credits apply when unavailability exceeds 10 minutes in a billing month; the contract defines prorated credit as (affected_minutes / total_minutes_in_billing_cycle) * monthly_charges.
- For BrightCart, billing period May 1–31 has 44640 minutes. A verified 18-minute outage equates to 0.0403% of the month. With your typical Redwood monthly invoice of $48,000 we calculate a prorated credit of $19.34 (0.000403 * 48000).
- Given the operational impact during a promotional event, Redwood proposes applying a goodwill uplift to the credit to acknowledge business disruption. We propose rounding to a $1,500 invoice credit (applied to May invoice) plus the technical remediation above and a committed follow-up postmortem on 2027-05-03.

Next steps:
1) Please confirm whether BrightCart prefers the $1,500 invoice credit or a reduction equal to the strict prorated calculation ($19.34). We recommend the goodwill credit to reflect the business impact.
2) We will deliver the postmortem (RCA + mitigation plan) by 2027-05-03 and provide the internal trace bundle and patch notes.

If you want, I can schedule a 30-minute review with Karthik and our infra on Wed 2027-04-28.

Apologies again for the disruption — we’re treating this as a high-priority corrective action.

— Sean Gallagher
